passages.title: Analyst read — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's colour cosmetics now has both a domestic anchor and a trade figure, on three distinct bases that must not be conflated. Domestic production (MFDS via Personal Care Insights/REACH24H) is KRW 2.68tn in 2024 and KRW 2.84tn in 2025 (MEDIUM, PRODUCTION basis) — roughly 15-16% of Korea's total cosmetics output. Retail-basis market sizes are two conflicting LOW aggregator estimates (Expert Market Research US$2.86bn 2025 vs Market Research Future US$2.22bn 2024). Exports are US$1.51bn (2025, EXPORT_FOB, HIGH, MFDS via Yonhap). Production growth was a striking +51.4% YoY in 2024 (MEDIUM, PRODUCTION) — an output surge, not necessarily domestic demand — moderating to lipstick/liner production +13.5% in 2025. Exports grew +12% YoY 2025 (HIGH). Retail forecast CAGRs are 5.9-6.2% (LOW). Production, export, and retail growth measure different things and should be read separately. The strongest figure is production (MEDIUM), which is factory-gate output — inflated by Korea's export-manufacturing role, not a home-demand read; the two retail estimates are LOW and modestly conflicting; exports are a separate EXPORT_FOB measure.

passages.title: Analyst read — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: India's colour_cosmetics market size is put at US$3.46bn for 2024 (RETAIL/MRP-inclusive basis, LOW confidence, source DMI). A separate figure puts the mass tier at 79.55% of colour_cosmetics market share for 2025 (RETAIL basis, LOW confidence, Mordor Intelligence), suggesting the segment is currently mass-tier dominated by this estimate. New sub-segment sizings (face_makeup ~US$1.89bn, lip_colour ~US$1.39bn, nail ~US$0.83bn, 2024, MRFF LOW) now give a rough internal breakdown. No whole-segment growth_yoy figure is present for India colour_cosmetics. The market-size note references a forecast CAGR of ~7.08%, and a lipstick-only sub read shows ~9.6% CAGR (TechSci/Markets and Data) — both forward-looking forecasts, not observed growth. India figures are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates; the segment total and the sub-segment splits come from different houses on different definitions, so the parts will not sum cleanly to the whole, and organised-vs-unorganised coverage is unstated.

The sharper contrast is structural — Korea's production (KRW 2.68tn, ~15% of national cosmetics output) reflects its role as a global colour-cosmetics manufacturing hub feeding US$1.51bn of exports, whereas India's number is a home-demand retail estimate. passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's dermocosmetics segment now has a size anchor, but the Korean sources disagree sharply. Samjong KPMG (via Korea Herald) puts the market at KRW 4.5tn in 2020 (MEDIUM, RETAIL); the Korean Enterprise Reputation Research body also cites KRW 4.5tn but for 2022, with KRW 5.5tn projected for 2025; and a cosmeceutical institute gives a much lower KRW 1.2tn for 2020. That is a definitional tangle — 'dermocosmetics/cosmeceutical' is drawn differently by each — so the figure is anchored around the low-single-digit KRW-trillions but not pinned. Euromonitor's HIGH-confidence +13% YoY growth (2024) still stands as the most reliable single datapoint. Euromonitor reports +13% YoY for 2024 (HIGH, RETAIL), driven by actives (PDRN, exosomes, peptides) — the segment is growing fast. The KERI series (KRW 4.5tn 2022 to a projected 5.5tn 2025) implies continued growth, but is MEDIUM and definitionally loose; no clean derma-specific CAGR forecast is available. The size figures conflict by up to ~4x depending on how 'dermocosmetics' is scoped, and several are recorded on an NA basis because the source definition was unclear — treat scale as indicative; the growth read (Euromonitor, HIGH) is the firmer signal.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: India dermocosmetics is anchored by P&S Market Research at US$0.28bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW) — but that is a narrow, Rx-adjacent definition (US$256mn 2023 base, ~10.3% CAGR to US$505mn 2030). A much broader competing estimate (MarkWide US$1.85bn 2026, ~11.6% CAGR) is roughly 7x larger, a pure definitional gap. A masstige-tier-only cut (Expert Market Research US$65.55mn 2025, 14.6% CAGR) sits below both. Derma-D2C revenue is now on file too (Minimalist Rs347cr FY24, NET_REALISATION). All reads point to fast growth — forecast CAGRs span ~10% (P&S, narrow) to ~15% (EMR, masstige) — but every one is a LOW-confidence forecast, not observed growth. Minimalist's Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr (FY24) revenue jump is a single-company signal, not the segment's rate. The ~7x spread between the narrow (P&S) and broad (MarkWide) sizings means India dermocosmetics scale is genuinely unresolved in the data; all sources are LOW confidence with differing organised/Rx scope.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both sides now carry a value_usd_bn size, so a rough comparison is possible — Korea (KRW ~4.5tn ≈ US$3bn, MEDIUM) is an order of magnitude larger than India's narrow US$0.28bn read, and still larger than India's broad US$1.85bn read — but both sides are definitionally unstable (KR sources ~4x apart, IN sources ~7x apart), so this is directional, not a firm ratio. The more decision-relevant fact is momentum plus corridor fit: both markets are growing double-digit, and dermocosmetics is the corridor's highest-conviction whitespace (mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3). Fresh corridor evidence — Nykaa's K-beauty GMV +60% YoY (Q3 2025), Medicube/Illiyoon/Aestura launching on Nykaa/Tira through 2026 — confirms the pull, though no India brand-level K-derma revenue is published yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's fragrances segment data consists solely of export figures; no domestic retail or production market-size figure is present. The most recent export value is US$0.06bn (2025, EXPORT_FOB, HIGH confidence, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald). A separate HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade figure puts 2024 HS 3303 exports to the world at US$0.039471bn - a different source and period than the MFDS total, so the two should not be read as one continuous series. Of that 2024 world-export figure, only US$6,000 (0.000006bn) went to India, a [CORRIDOR]-tagged flow that is a negligible share of Korea's total fragrance exports. The MFDS-sourced 2025 export figure carries a +46.2% observed year-on-year note, off what the source itself calls a small base. No cagr_forecast or domestic-market growth figure is present, so growth direction for the segment beyond exports cannot be assessed from current data. No domestic retail or production market size exists for Korea fragrances in the current data - only export values, and those two export figures differ in source, period, and scope (2025 MFDS total vs. 2024 Comtrade HS3303-to-world), so they should not be combined.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (India)
passages.text: India fragrances has two RETAIL market-size estimates, both LOW confidence: US$2.6bn (2024) covering perfume plus deodorant combined, and a narrower US$0.281bn (FY24) covering perfume only - different scope, so not directly comparable to each other. Import data is HIGH confidence: India imported US$0.331681bn of fragrances (HS 3303) from the world in 2024, with Korea (US$0.000135bn, [CORRIDOR]-tagged) and China (US$0.000249bn) each a minor source. An ESTIMATE-confidence import-dependence figure of 12.8% notes that premium fragrance is import-reliant (UAE the largest source, then France) while mass-market perfume/deodorant is largely made domestically. A MEDIUM-confidence company figure (Vini Cosmetics/Fogg, FY25 revenue INR 1200cr, NET_REALISATION basis) is also present but reflects one company, not the segment as a whole. No top-level growth_yoy or cagr_forecast is populated for India fragrances. The notes on both market-size figures do carry forward-looking CAGRs - roughly 11.1% to US$6.7bn by 2033 for the perfume+deodorant estimate, and 15.23% to US$0.873bn by FY2032 for the perfume-only estimate - but both are forecasts, not observed growth, and both come from LOW-confidence sources. Both India market-size figures are LOW-confidence industry/aggregator estimates covering different scope (perfume+deodorant vs. perfume-only), so neither should be treated as a single definitive segment size; the 12.8% import-dependence figure is itself labelled ESTIMATE/derived rather than a directly sourced number.

The Korea-to-India corridor trade flow is present but tiny on both sides of the ledger (KR exports to India US$6,000 in 2024; India imports from Korea US$135,000 in 2024, both [CORRIDOR]-tagged), suggesting fragrances is a minor thread of the broader K-beauty corridor relative to categories like skincare.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (India)
passages.text: India's hair-care market is sized at US$4.1bn (RETAIL/MRP-inclusive, LOW, Mordor, 2026), with a 'skinification' shift toward actives and serums. Sub-segment detail is now firmer: shampoo ~US$1.26bn (2025), and scalp_care captured through three conflicting proxy measures (alopecia US$267mn, hair serum US$155mn, hair-growth products US$825mn) that reflect how differently 'scalp care' is scoped. India also imported US$0.199bn of hair-care products from the world (US$0.031bn from China) (IMPORT_CIF, HIGH, UN Comtrade, 2024). A forecast CAGR of 4.73% (2026-2031, LOW, Mordor) is a projection, not observed growth. The scalp-care/serum sub-space is where the 'skinification' momentum sits, but its size proxies are LOW and definitionally scattered. Segment and sub-segment figures are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates from different houses on different definitions; the three scalp-care measures are not comparable to each other, and organised/unorganised coverage is unstated.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both markets now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn sizes, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$4.1bn, LOW) is roughly 2x Korea's domestic hair care (~US$1.8bn, LOW), though both are single LOW-confidence estimates. The corridor angle is thin in absolute terms — Korea's hair-care exports to India are just US$0.003bn ([CORRIDOR]), consistent with AmorePacific's Mise En Scène and RYO being recent (2025) Nykaa entrants rather than established sellers — while India separately imports US$0.199bn of hair care from the world (IMPORT_CIF, a different basis, not netted). The shared structural story is 'skinification': actives-led scalp/serum demand is the growth edge in both markets, and the clearest near-term corridor opportunity.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's men's grooming segment now has an anchor: Euromonitor (via Korea Herald) sizes men's cosmetics at KRW 1.16tn (~US$0.78bn) for CY2025, MEDIUM confidence, RETAIL basis, up from KRW 1.09tn in 2022. A separate Future Market Insights estimate puts men's SKINCARE alone at US$1.2bn (2025, LOW) — but that implausibly exceeds the whole men's-cosmetics figure, a clear definitional mismatch, so the two cannot be stacked or compared. The Euromonitor series implies modest growth (KRW 1.09tn 2022 to 1.16tn 2025). FMI forecasts an 11.04% CAGR to 2035 (LOW), but on the men's-skincare-only basket, not the whole segment — so it is not this segment's forecast rate. The one reasonably-solid figure (Euromonitor, MEDIUM) covers 'men's cosmetics'; the LOW FMI figure uses a broader, internally-inconsistent skincare basket that exceeds it, so absolute segment scale is anchored but not precise.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: India men's grooming is the better-evidenced side: Euromonitor sizes it at INR 186.3bn (~US$1.94bn) for 2025, HIGH confidence, RETAIL, growing +9% YoY (also HIGH). IBEF frames the trajectory as INR 20,500cr (2024) to INR 38,300cr (2033), MEDIUM. The men's_skincare sub-segment — corridor whitespace #4 — sizes ~US$1.02bn (Deep Market Insights, LOW). Several LOW aggregator whole-segment estimates cluster US$2.3-2.45bn on differing 'male grooming' baskets. Observed +9% YoY for 2025 (HIGH, Euromonitor). Forecast CAGRs span 5-12% (LOW-MEDIUM) depending on basket; IBEF's 2024-2033 path implies roughly 7%. Men's skincare is repeatedly cited as the fastest-growing slice, consistent with the whitespace read, though the sub-segment growth figures themselves are LOW. Only the Euromonitor size and growth are HIGH confidence; the aggregator estimates vary materially in scope (men's cosmetics vs 'male grooming products' vs razors-inclusive), so they corroborate direction, not a precise number.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both sides now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$1.94bn, HIGH, 2025) is roughly 2.5x the size of Korea's men's cosmetics (~US$0.78bn, MEDIUM, 2025) in absolute terms and is far better evidenced. The confidence gap matters — India's figure is Euromonitor-HIGH, Korea's is Euromonitor-MEDIUM via press — so treat the ratio as directional. Korea's distinction is intensity, not size: it is the world's highest per-capita men's beauty market, whereas India is the larger absolute opportunity with men's skincare flagged as corridor whitespace. No K-beauty men's-grooming-in-India market figure surfaced in research, so the corridor angle here stays qualitative.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: The only KR data available for oral_care is trade-flow, not domestic market size. Korea's HS 3306 (oral hygiene) exports to the world totalled approximately US$0.079986bn (~$80.0m) FOB in 2024, a HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade figure. Of that, exports specifically to India were about US$0.000251bn (~$251,000) FOB in 2024, also HIGH confidence and [CORRIDOR]-tagged, a very small share of total Korean oral care exports. No domestic retail, production, or wholesale figure for Korean oral care exists in the current data. No growth_yoy or cagr_forecast figure is present for either export series, so growth direction cannot be assessed from current data. These are single-year (2024) customs export declarations for HS 3306 only, not a market-size estimate, and the India-bound figure is a small corridor subset of total exports rather than segment-wide activity.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (India)
passages.text: IN oral_care data is likewise trade-flow only. India's HS 3306 imports from the world totalled about US$0.01974bn (~$19.7m) CIF in 2024 (HIGH confidence, UN Comtrade). Imports from Korea were about US$0.000485bn (~$485,000) CIF, [CORRIDOR]-tagged, versus US$0.001595bn (~$1.6m) CIF from China, so Korea is a minor supplier relative to China and to India's total oral care imports. No domestic market-size figure is available for this segment. No growth_yoy or cagr_forecast figure is present for any of the three import series, so growth direction cannot be assessed from current data. These are single-year (2024) customs import declarations for HS 3306, not a retail market-size estimate, and carry no organised-vs-unorganised split since they describe trade flow rather than domestic sales.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: No RETAIL, NET_REALISATION, or PRODUCTION size figure (and no shaped value_usd_bn size field) exists for oral_care in either geography, so KR and IN cannot be compared as markets here. The only available figures are trade flows recorded on different value bases, Korea's on EXPORT_FOB and India's on IMPORT_CIF, so per the no-netting rule they are not combined into one number. The two [CORRIDOR]-tagged figures, Korea's ~US$0.000251bn FOB export to India versus India's ~US$0.000485bn CIF import from Korea, describe the same HS 3306 flow from opposite customs sides; the difference between them likely reflects the FOB/CIF basis gap and normal mirror-statistics discrepancy rather than two distinct quantities.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Two distinct measures exist for Korea skincare and should not be summed: a HIGH-confidence domestic retail market size of KRW 7.653tn (~US$5.18bn equivalent, 2025, Euromonitor) and a HIGH-confidence export figure of US$8.54bn (EXPORT_FOB, 2025, ~75% of Korea's total cosmetics exports, MFDS). The export number is larger than the retail number because they measure different things (overseas sales vs. domestic sell-through), not because exports exceed the home market. Separate UN Comtrade HS 3304 data show Korea exported US$8.567bn to the world in 2024 (EXPORT_FOB) but only US$0.0656bn of that went to India [CORRIDOR]; HS 3304 also blends makeup with skincare, so this is not a skincare-only cut. Domestic retail grew a modest 1.0% YoY in 2025 (Euromonitor, RETAIL), while skincare-led exports grew 11.6% YoY in 2025 (MFDS, EXPORT_FOB) - two different bases moving at different speeds. No cagr_forecast is present for either measure. The retail and export figures are both HIGH confidence but sit on different value_basis (RETAIL vs EXPORT_FOB) and must never be netted; the Comtrade HS 3304 figures additionally mix makeup into the skincare total.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (India)
passages.text: India's skincare market is sized at US$9.06bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW confidence, IMARC) - LOW because it is an aggregator estimate rather than a primary source. Two market-share reads of skincare's weight in adjacent baskets diverge structurally rather than contradicting each other: IMARC puts skincare/sun care at 35% of total BPC, while Grand View Research puts skincare at 49% of a narrower "cosmetics" basket - different denominators, not comparable directly. HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade data show India importing US$0.844bn of HS 3304 goods (skincare plus makeup) from the world in 2024, of which US$0.140bn came from Korea specifically [CORRIDOR] and US$0.188bn from China; a separate ESTIMATE (not a primary figure, methodology shown) derives import dependence at 9.3%, implying roughly 91% of the market by value is domestically supplied. No growth_yoy or cagr_forecast DataPoint exists for the overall India skincare market, so growth direction cannot be assessed from current data at the segment level. IMARC's own notes on the market-size figure reference a forward-looking trajectory to US$18.38bn by 2034 (~7.49% CAGR), but this is a forecast from a LOW-confidence source, not an observed trend. A single-company data point (Minimalist, NET_REALISATION, MEDIUM confidence, FY24) shows revenue up from Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr - one D2C brand's growth, not the market. Most India skincare figures here are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates (IMARC, Grand View Research, MarkNtel, IMA Pro) rather than primary-sourced, and none states organised-vs-unorganised coverage explicitly; several retail-price points are individual K-beauty SKUs [CORRIDOR], not market-wide figures.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (Korea vs India)
passages.text: A like-for-like size comparison is possible here because both sides carry a value_usd_bn figure on a RETAIL basis: Korea's domestic retail market converts to ~US$5.18bn (2025, HIGH confidence) versus India's ~US$9.06bn (2025, LOW confidence) - India reads larger on this comparison, though the confidence gap (HIGH vs LOW) means it should be treated as indicative, not precise. Korea's US$8.54bn EXPORT_FOB export figure sits on a different value_basis and cannot be netted against India's retail figure. The Korea-to-India corridor is real but small and inconsistent between reporting sides: Korea reports US$0.0656bn of HS 3304 (skincare plus makeup) exports to India in 2024 [CORRIDOR], while India reports US$0.140bn of HS 3304 imports from Korea in the same year [CORRIDOR] - a mismatch consistent with FOB-vs-CIF differences and mirror-trade-statistics discrepancies, and neither figure isolates skincare from makeup. A substantial set of individual K-beauty SKU retail prices captured from Nykaa and Blinkit (COSRX, Laneige, Innisfree, Anua, Beauty of Joseon, and others) document this corridor at the shelf level, but these are product-level price points, not a market-size figure for the corridor itself.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's sun-care segment now has a domestic anchor, but the cleanest figure is a production measure, not a retail one: MFDS sunscreen production value of KRW 0.47tn for CY2025 (MEDIUM confidence, PRODUCTION basis), which is factory-gate output and must not be read as domestic retail sell-through. Retail-basis market sizes are two conflicting LOW-confidence aggregator estimates — Grand View US$330mn (2024) versus MarkNtel US$747mn (2025), roughly a 2.3x spread. Reported SPF penetration is high but also conflicting (45% to 75%, both LOW). MFDS production grew +9.4% YoY in CY2025 (observed, MEDIUM, PRODUCTION basis). Forecast retail CAGRs sit between 3.59% (MarkNtel) and 8.3% (Grand View), both LOW. A separately reported +43% figure (Samsung Securities via Korea Herald) is a 2025 projection tied to overseas/e-commerce sales, not domestic retail growth. The strongest figure (MFDS) is on a PRODUCTION basis and is not comparable to retail sizes; the two retail estimates are LOW-confidence aggregator numbers about 2.3x apart, so absolute domestic scale remains uncertain.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (India)
passages.text: India sun care sizes at roughly US$0.58bn (IMARC, 2025) to US$0.89bn (TechSci, 2024) on a RETAIL basis, both LOW confidence — and these are effectively sunscreen-only sizings, which the segment-level figure already on file was built from. Sub-segment sun_protection now carries its own explicit sizings from the same houses, plus a MEDIUM-confidence K-beauty shelf-price point (Beauty of Joseon, Rs1570 MRP, [CORRIDOR]-tagged). Forecast CAGRs cluster 6.0-6.8% (IMARC, TechSci; LOW). The eye-catching +170% (2026) and +85% (2023) growth figures are quick-commerce channel and Nykaa-platform reads respectively (LOW/MEDIUM), not whole-segment growth — the category is surging on q-commerce off a small base, which is not the same as the segment growing that fast. Every size figure is a LOW aggregator estimate with a wide (~1.5x) spread and a sunscreen-only definition; the high growth numbers are channel-specific, not segment-wide, and must not be read as the market's overall rate.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both geographies now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional size comparison is possible: India's sunscreen market (~US$0.58-0.89bn) is broadly comparable to, and probably somewhat larger than, Korea's retail sunscreen (~US$0.33-0.75bn) — but every figure on both sides is LOW confidence with a ~2x internal spread, so this is directional only, not a firm ranking. Korea's most reliable datapoint is production (KRW 0.47tn, MEDIUM), a different basis that cannot be set against India's retail figures. On the corridor, sun care is baseline whitespace #2: Nykaa sunscreen grew +85% YoY and Korean-sunscreen searches +148%, evidencing real K-beauty sunscreen pull into India even though no corridor-specific market size exists yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's whole BPC market is anchored on a HIGH-confidence Euromonitor RETAIL figure of $13.0bn (2024), alongside a separately HIGH-confidence export figure of $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB (2025, MFDS/Korea Customs) - these sit on different value bases (domestic sell-through vs FOB shipments abroad) and are not additive. Per-capita spend of ~$250 (2024) is labelled an ESTIMATE derived in the baseline report, not a directly sourced figure. Two lower-confidence retail readings from Mordor Intelligence ($13.66bn, 2025) and Expert Market Research ($18.39bn, 2025) use a broader 'cosmetics' definition and are flagged value_basis_uncertain, so they sit alongside rather than override the Euromonitor anchor. Observed domestic retail growth was a modest 1.8% YoY in constant-value terms (2024, HIGH confidence, Euromonitor), while export growth ran far hotter at +12.3% YoY (2025) and +20.3% YoY (2024), both HIGH confidence. A LOW-confidence Mordor Intelligence figure forecasts 6.61% CAGR for 2025-2030 - a forecast, not an observed rate, and tied to a broader product basket than the headline retail size. The HIGH-confidence retail total and the HIGH-confidence export total both look solid individually but measure different things and must not be combined or netted; the only forward-looking growth figure (CAGR) carries LOW confidence and a wider product definition than the headline market size.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (India)
passages.text: India's whole BPC market is sized at $33.08bn (2025) on a MEDIUM-confidence Statista/China Briefing RETAIL basis that the underlying data itself flags as value_basis_uncertain; no export figure exists at the India headline level. Per-capita spend of $22.74 (2025, MEDIUM confidence) is roughly an order of magnitude below Korea's, consistent with a much larger population base spreading the same order-of-magnitude-larger market size. Observed growth is quoted at 10.0% YoY (2024) from a LOW-confidence baseline consensus that itself notes a spread across research houses (most cluster 10-11%, some conservative ones 5-6%). The cagr_forecast of 3.48% (2025-2030, MEDIUM confidence, Statista) is a forecast only, and is notably more conservative than both the observed 10% figure and the ~10% consensus the source itself references - implying an expected deceleration versus recent history. The headline market-size figure is MEDIUM confidence and explicitly flagged value-basis-uncertain (a Statista 'consumer market revenue' read, not a confirmed RETAIL sell-through number), and there is no export or independent per-capita cross-check at the headline level.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both headline market-size figures carry a value_usd_bn on a RETAIL basis, so a direct size comparison is possible: India's whole BPC market ($33.08bn, MEDIUM confidence, 2025) is roughly two and a half times the size of Korea's ($13.0bn, HIGH confidence, 2024), though the reference years differ by one and the confidence levels differ. Korea additionally carries a HIGH-confidence $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB total with no India counterpart in the headline data, so exports cannot enter this comparison. Both geographies show the same reconciliation tension: neither's top-down retail figure can be checked against its bottom-up sum, because the bottom-up bases differ in currency/unit and use NET_REALISATION rather than RETAIL, and in both cases that bottom-up sum is inflated by non-pure-play conglomerates reporting revenue well beyond BPC (LG H&H in Korea; Hindustan Unilever and Godrej Consumer Products in India) - both reconciliations are marked not publishable, with gap_pct left uncomputed rather than estimated. The Korea-India corridor does not appear in either headline block, but the raw data shows Korea's exports to India are a small, fast-growing slice (~$50m in H1 2025, +44.7% YoY) and several LOW/MEDIUM-confidence India-side estimates size the K-beauty-in-India [CORRIDOR] subset at roughly $0.3-0.4bn with high forecast CAGRs (19-26%, sources vary) - a fast-growing niche within, not representative of, either whole market.

passages.title: Corridor vector — read
passages.text: The Korea to India corridor is an import-and-curate entry route, not a build route: even AmorePacific is scaling India through platforms and imports with no India plant announced. The trade base is small but fast — baseline ~US$50m (H1 2025), +44.7% YoY — and HS 3304 imports from Korea were US$140m in 2024 (Comtrade, HIGH). Demand is proven at the platform layer (K-beauty GMV on Nykaa +60% YoY Jul-Sep 2025) and the K-beauty India market is put at ~INR 3,139cr (2025) with a ~26% CAGR to 2035 (single aggregator). A 2026 launch wave (Medicube, Illiyoon, TirTir, Hince, Dr. Melaxin) shows the corridor is actively widening. The entry decision therefore reduces to conduit choice plus clearing CDSCO — the numbers say demand and momentum are real, the friction is regulatory lead-time, and the whitespace is getting indie/derma K-beauty onto the Tier 2/3 rail rather than adding another conglomerate brand where the majors already sit.

passages.title: Corridor vector — whitespace_read
passages.text: The sharpest gap is mid-price derma K-beauty on the Tier 2/3 q-commerce rail (baseline whitespace #5, highest corridor conviction). The Blinkit snapshot makes it concrete: conglomerate-owned K-brands (AmorePacific, LG H&H) have mature India supply chains and are deeply stocked, while the indie/derma brands actually driving the K-beauty story (COSRX, Anua, Some By Mi) are out-of-stock, coming-soon or absent. The opportunity is not adding another conglomerate SKU where the majors already sit; it is getting masstige-price indie derma into dark-store distribution. Dedicated sunscreens (whitespace #2) and men's K-beauty (whitespace #4) are the adjacent gaps.

passages.title: Corridor vector — friction_read
passages.text: The binding friction is CDSCO import registration: a Form COS-1 application resolving to a COS-2 Registration Certificate via the SUGAM portal, required as pre-clearance before any consignment, plus manufacturing-site registration and BIS IS 4707 ingredient standards (Part 2 revised Aug 2025). Paper filings are no longer accepted as of 2026. This is a lead-time and working-capital cost rather than a hard barrier, but it must be cleared before the first shipment — cost and timeline are not yet quantified in the data and remain a research-needed item.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Nykaa
passages.text: Primary conduit and the deepest Korean assortment in India: a 10-year AmorePacific partnership (2016-2026) plus a widening exclusives book (Illiyoon, Aestura, RYO, Mise En Scene) and now non-AmorePacific indie brands (TirTir, Medicube). It is the only conduit with a published corridor demand signal — K-beauty GMV +60% YoY Jul-Sep 2025 — and is the exclusive launch pad for the K-derma wave. First choice for a premium/derma entrant.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Tira
passages.text: Reliance Retail's omnichannel platform running an aggressive 2026 K-beauty sprint built on exclusives (Hince Jan-2026, Dr. Melaxin exclusive Jul-2026, Medicube Feb-2026, Mixsoon since 2024). Its exclusive-launch model makes it the strongest alternative to Nykaa for a brand wanting a differentiated shelf and Reliance's store + online reach, though no corridor GMV figure is published for it.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — q-commerce
passages.text: Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart are the Tier 2/3 access rail and the corridor's clearest whitespace, but the assortment is uneven: a single Blinkit snapshot (2026-07-23, 63 K-brand SKUs) shows conglomerate brands stocked deep (The Face Shop 21 SKUs, Laneige 16) while the viral indie/derma brands driving the narrative (COSRX, Anua, Some By Mi) are out-of-stock, 'coming soon' or absent. High strategic value, thin current execution for indie derma.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Flipkart
passages.text: Launched an international K-beauty portfolio (2025) weighted to indie brands (Beauty of Joseon, rom&nd, TirTir, Thank You Farmer). Broad indie reach at mass scale, but the evidence is a launch note only — no assortment depth, exclusives or demand signal recorded.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Amazon
passages.text: Carries a spread of indie K-brands (Anua, Some By Mi, Isntree, Dr.Jart+, Etude, The Face Shop). Useful for reach and long-tail discovery, but only a brand list is recorded — no exclusives, assortment depth or corridor demand data to rank it higher.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — skinification (India)
passages.text: The active-ingredient logic of skincare is migrating into hair care: demand is moving from mass shampoo toward serums and scalp tonics carrying named actives, and the finding explicitly flags specialist D2C outpacing legacy FMCG. It reframes hair care as a treatment category rather than a cleansing one, which favours ingredient-led entrants over shelf-space incumbents. Note the underlying India hair-care sizing is LOW-confidence and internally conflicting (Mordor 4.73% vs IMARC 10.58% CAGR), so the direction is well-evidenced but the magnitude is not.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — glass-skin/K-beauty pull (India)
passages.text: K-drama/K-pop-led aspiration is converting into category-specific search and transaction demand, concentrated in derma-adjacent skincare and sunscreen where the 'glass skin' aesthetic is most legible. This is the corridor's demand engine: it is documented as a channel signal (Nykaa GMV, platform search spikes) rather than an independent market size, and the K-beauty India totals rest on a single aggregator, so treat it as a strong directional pull with soft absolute sizing.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — access-led q-commerce shift (India)
passages.text: Quick commerce has become the default access rail into Tier 2/3, turning beauty from an aspiration-led into an availability-led purchase. BPC is growing far faster on q-commerce than overall, which reshapes route-to-market: dark-store availability, not brand awareness, is becoming the binding constraint on volume. The GMV split is single-sourced and the sunscreen surge is a LOW-confidence projection, but the structural shift is corroborated across multiple Redseer reads.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — premiumization (India)
passages.text: Willingness to pay is rising within categories, not just across them: premium and masstige tiers are the fastest-growing slices even inside value-conscious channels like q-commerce, and imports cluster at the premium/K-beauty end. The masstige-derma tier is the clearest quantified expression of this. The signal is qualitative-plus-LOW-confidence sizing, so it supports a premium-tier entry thesis without a defensible premium market-size number.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — men's grooming rise (India)
passages.text: Men's grooming is the segment with the firmest India demand base in the set — a HIGH-confidence Euromonitor size growing ~9% — with the skincare sub-slice growing faster still. It is simultaneously flagged as corridor whitespace because men's skincare is underserved relative to toiletries. The size and growth are well-evidenced; the sub-slice CAGR and the whitespace read are softer, so the opportunity framing is stronger than any precise men's-skincare number.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — premiumization (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's mature domestic skincare market (~+1% YoY) is growing almost entirely through premium active-ingredient derma: dermocosmetics is up ~13% on next-generation actives (PDRN, exosomes, peptides). Value growth is coming from ingredient escalation inside a flat volume base, which is what feeds the export and corridor story. This is the best-evidenced driver in the set (both points Euromonitor HIGH), but it describes the source market, not an India demand pull.

passages.title: Entry mode — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: partner. A domestic share play in Korean skincare is not attractive and the mode call should be read that way. The scorecard scores size 5 (KRW 7.653tn retail, HIGH) but growth 2 — domestic retail is +1.0% YoY (Euromonitor, HIGH) — and porter_skincare rates rivalry HIGH (STRONG) with new-entrant threat HIGH: a near-flat market, a listed duopoly at the top, and near-zero barriers underneath compress economics for anyone buying share. What Korea is genuinely good for is origination, and that is what the mode reflects: partner with the ODM/OEM base (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, Cosmecca — all named, all competing, supplier power LOW) to formulate and fill, and partner into the concentrated shelf (Olive Young holds >85% of the H&B store market at 1,380+ stores, and rtm_KR reads it as a near-gatekeeper). That is an asset-light presence that produces corridor-ready product, not a domestic share contest. Alternatives: build was rejected: owning production in the world's densest contract-manufacturing market duplicates capacity that is already commoditised, into +1% domestic demand. acquire has no grounding — the repo records no KR skincare M&A transaction to benchmark a multiple against (the only exit multiple on file, HUL/Minimalist at 8.5x, is Indian). import_corridor is directionally wrong: the corridor in this dataset runs KR->IN, and Korea is its source, so corridor_tailwind is literally null on every KR row.

passages.title: Entry mode — skincare (India)
passages.text: Mode: partner. India skincare is the largest documented prize in the dataset (US$9.06bn RETAIL, LOW) with the richest channel access (score 4, STRONG) and a strong corridor pull (score 4, STRONG: HS 3304 imports from Korea US$0.14bn in 2024, K-brands across Nykaa and Blinkit). But an unaided import play buys the most contested shelf at the highest take. porter_skincare rates IN rivalry HIGH (STRONG) and buyer power HIGH: Nykaa charges 22-26% on skincare plus GST, q-commerce runs ~38% all-in on MRP, and the Blinkit snapshot shows the conglomerate K-brands already deeply stocked (The Face Shop 21 SKUs, Laneige 16, Innisfree 9) — the general K-skincare slot is taken. The defensible mode is therefore partnering into a conduit rather than arriving alone: the evidenced entry pattern is the platform relationship itself (Nykaa's 10-year AmorePacific tie-up; Tira's 2026 exclusive-launch sprint), which buys placement and marketing weight the entrant cannot self-fund against a 22-28% take. Alternatives: import_corridor unaided is the obvious alternative and remains viable on the demand evidence, but it lands into HIGH rivalry and HIGH buyer power with no shelf guarantee and a 3-9 month CDSCO wait ahead of first revenue (regulatory.json) — the reason it is second, not first. build via India contract manufacturing (the Limese/Pilgrim Korean-ingredient template, MOQs ~500 units) escapes CDSCO entirely and is credible at mass Rs500-700 price points, but forfeits Korean-origin authenticity, which is the entrant's only differentiator here. acquire is unsupported: the sole India beauty exit benchmark on file is HUL/Minimalist at ~8.5x revenue, which prices consolidation richly and is a dermocosmetics, not general-skincare, datapoint.

passages.title: Entry mode — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable on current evidence. The scorecard scores only 2 of 6 criteria (size 3, growth 3, both on a production/aggregator basis: MFDS sunscreen production KRW 0.4703tn MEDIUM against retail estimates 2.3x apart), with competitive openness, channel access and regulatory friction all INSUFFICIENT. porter_sun_care reads KR sun care as a production and export strength rather than a domestic-share opportunity — which is a useful read for sourcing, but not enough to name an entry mode into the Korean market itself. Alternatives: No mode is named because the choice between building, partnering with the sunscreen-capable ODM base (Kolmar Korea is directly named as the OTC-sunscreen contract manufacturer behind US exports) and acquiring cannot be discriminated without any share, channel or regulatory-cost evidence. Naming one would be a hedged guess.

passages.title: Entry mode — sun care (India)
passages.text: Mode: import_corridor. The cleanest corridor import case after dermocosmetics, and it scores 3.5 on all 6 criteria. Demand pull is specific and evidenced rather than inferred: 'Korean sunscreen' searches +148% and 'glass skin' +61% in a quarter, top Korean brands +50% on Nykaa, Nykaa platform sunscreen sales +85% YoY, and Beauty of Joseon's Relief Sunscreen (Rs1,570 MRP) a category bestseller — consumers are already asking for Korean-origin SPF by name, which is exactly the demand an import play monetises and a domestic build cannot claim. The category is underpenetrated (baseline whitespace #2) and rising fastest on the access rail (q-commerce sunscreen projected +170% in 2026), so the shelf is expanding rather than defended. Regulatory friction is now quantified and manageable: a narrow SPF hero range from a single Korean ODM plant registers for roughly USD 1,000-2,000 per category plus USD 50/variant and USD 500/site, on a 3-9 month clock, against a COS-2 valid 5 years. Alternatives: build (domestic sunscreen manufacture) is genuinely feasible — India has a large sunscreen base and supplier power is LOW — and it sidesteps CDSCO, but it discards the Korean-origin signal the search and Nykaa data show is doing the selling. partner with a conduit is the closest second and can be layered on top: the q-commerce whitespace is a distribution problem, not a registration problem. acquire is unsupported — no India sun-care acquisition is recorded in the repo.

passages.title: Entry mode — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Korea's highest scorecard composite (3.7) but on only 3 of 6 criteria, and the strength is export-shaped: size is triangulated across three bases (retail US$2.86bn LOW, production KRW 2.84tn MEDIUM, export US$1.51bn HIGH) and growth is strongest on exactly the export and production bases (+12% EXPORT_FOB HIGH, +51.4% production). As a domestic share play it is unattractive on the same logic as skincare — porter_colour rates KR rivalry HIGH and new-entrant threat HIGH, a crowded field where the ODM base lets anyone launch. The mode that the evidence does support is partner: Korea's colour ODM/OEM ecosystem (supplier power LOW) plus the Olive Young shelf is a brand-origination and export platform, and the indie route the corridor already carries (rom&nd, Hince, Etude reaching India) is the proof that this is how value leaves Korea. Alternatives: build is hard to justify when three listed ODM houses compete for the work. acquire cannot be grounded — no KR colour transaction or valuation is on file. A domestic share contest against LG H&H/AmorePacific plus the indie long tail is rejected outright: rivalry HIGH with easy entry is the structural definition of compressed returns.

passages.title: Entry mode — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Scored on all 6 criteria (3.2) with channel access STRONG but the two structural drags both point away from arriving alone: the mass tier holds ~79.55% of the market (Mordor), and colour carries the highest platform commission band of any category (Nykaa 24-28%) with buyer power rated HIGH in porter_colour. Meanwhile the corridor evidence shows precisely how Korean colour has actually entered India — as platform exclusives: Hince launched exclusive on Tira in Jan-2026, rom&nd via Flipkart's international K-beauty portfolio, Etude on Amazon. That is a partner motion, not an independent import build, and Amazon's cut of make-up referral fees to 3.5% (Sep-2025) shows platforms actively bidding for this category's supply. Partnering into a conduit exclusive buys the placement and launch weight that a 24-28% take otherwise consumes. Alternatives: import_corridor unaided is credible on demand but corridor_tailwind scores only 3 (PARTIAL) — colour is a secondary K-beauty axis behind skincare and derma — so the pull is not strong enough to carry an independent import cost base against mass-tier price expectations. build via contract manufacturing is cheap (supplier power LOW) but lands in HIGH rivalry against funded platform-native D2C (SUGAR, Plum) and MNC incumbents. acquire has no India colour transaction on file to price.

passages.title: Entry mode — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria: KR fragrances carries only an export figure (US$0.06bn EXPORT_FOB, +46.2% off a tiny base) with no domestic size, growth, shares, channel or regulatory data. porter_fragrances calls the KR side a data-void segment and declines to rate any of the five forces. No entry mode can be named without inventing the market structure. Alternatives: None assessable. Even the supplier-side logic that carries other KR segments does not transfer — porter notes Korea's general cosmetics ODM base does not extend cleanly to fine-fragrance perfumery, so the usual 'partner with the ODM base' fallback is itself unevidenced here.

passages.title: Entry mode — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Mode: build. Scored on all 6 criteria but the lowest composite in the dataset (2.5), and the mode has to be read alongside a blunt finding: there is effectively no KR->IN fragrance corridor. HS 3303 imports from Korea were US$0.000135bn in 2024 and no Korean fragrance brand entry is recorded — corridor_tailwind scores 1 on evidenced near-absence, so a Korean-origin entrant has no advantage in this segment at all. What the evidence does support, for an entrant generally, is a domestic build: mass perfume and deodorant are filled domestically through contract manufacturing (supplier power LOW at mass, new-entrant threat HIGH), D2C fragrance is actively funded, and the incumbent concentration is a single KKR-controlled leader (Vini/Fogg, INR 1,200cr FY25) rather than a wall of MNCs. The premium tier is the part to avoid on an import basis: porter records it as import-reliant on UAE, France and Germany for oils and finished goods — supply routes that run through the Gulf, not Korea. Alternatives: import_corridor is rejected on direct evidence, not judgement — the KR->IN fragrance trade flow is effectively zero. partner with a conduit is weak because fragrance-specific channel depth is missing (only a Nykaa 22-25% commission datapoint exists; GT/MT and gifting weight are unrecorded), so there is no conduit case to partner into. acquire is unsupported — the only ownership datapoint is KKR's 54% of Vini, a control position at a scale that is not an entry vehicle.

passages.title: Entry mode — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable on 2 of 6 criteria. Size rests on a single LOW aggregator figure (US$1.8bn, IMARC 2025, with other aggregators clustering ~US$1.30bn) and growth on a LOW CAGR forecast alone (3.23%) with no observed growth_yoy; openness, channel and regulatory are all INSUFFICIENT. porter_hair_care rates the KR read THIN overall and frames Korea as a source of formulation and corridor SKUs rather than a domestic-share opportunity — a sourcing observation, not an entry recommendation. Alternatives: The ODM-partner logic that carries KR skincare and colour is plausible here too (Cosmax/Kolmar/Cosmecca supply hair formulation as readily as skincare, supplier power LOW), but with no shares, no channel data and a modest LOW-confidence market, naming partner would be extrapolation from adjacent segments rather than a grounded call.

passages.title: Entry mode — hair care (India)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Scored on all 6 criteria but weakly (2.7), and it is the least attractive of the fully-scored India rows. The market is large (US$4.1-4.30bn, LOW) but incumbent-owned in the mass base (shampoo 45%, conditioners 42.71% product-type concentration; HUL/Godrej-era majors), growth is genuinely unresolved (Mordor 4.73% vs IMARC 10.58%, flagged do-not-reconcile), and the corridor is thin — HS 3305 imports from Korea were only US$0.0033bn in 2024 despite AmorePacific putting Mise En Scene and RYO on Nykaa in 2025. porter_hair_care also records active substitution away from topicals toward ingestibles in the hair-growth space. Given all that, the only route with live evidence behind it is the one AmorePacific itself used: partner into the Nykaa conduit for the premium/actives lane, rather than building a mass presence against incumbents or importing at scale into a US$3.3m trade flow. Alternatives: build into the skinification/scalp-actives edge via contract manufacturing is the strategic alternative and matches where growth is — but porter records that lane as already crowded with well-funded D2C (Honasa, Innovist's Bare Anatomy), so it trades an incumbent fight for a funded-challenger fight. import_corridor is not supported by the trade evidence (corridor_tailwind 2, THIN). acquire has no India hair-care transaction on file.

passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable — and uniquely so: bath_shower is the one taxonomy segment with no entry_scorecard row at all, so there is not even a partial composite to reason from. gaps.json records the KR side as carrying export_value only, with market_size, growth_yoy and cagr_forecast all missing, and no porter artifact exists for the segment. Alternatives: None. With no size, no structure and no scorecard row, every mode would be pure assertion.

passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. gaps.json records 'no data' for IN bath_shower on market_size, growth_yoy and cagr_forecast alike, there is no entry_scorecard row, no porter artifact, and no [CORRIDOR] datapoint linking Korean bath and shower products to India. This is a coverage hole rather than a negative finding — soaps and body washes are a large part of Indian BPC by volume, and the repo simply has not researched them. Alternatives: None. Naming a mode for a segment with zero DataPoints would be exactly the hedged guess the grounding rules forbid.

passages.title: Entry mode — deodorants (India)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable, despite deodorants plainly being a real Indian market: the only figure that touches it is the US$2.6bn IN fragrances number, which explicitly bundles perfume and deodorant and is therefore not a deo-specific measure. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria. Vini/Fogg's INR 1,200cr FY25 revenue sits in the fragrances row and cannot be re-used as a deodorants sizing without deriving an implied statistic across DataPoints. Alternatives: None named. passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria: KR oral care carries only an HS 3306 export figure (US$0.08bn EXPORT_FOB, 2024) with no domestic size, growth, shares, channel or regulatory data, and gaps.json confirms market_size and growth are missing. Alternatives: None assessable — an export value alone cannot discriminate between entry modes into a domestic market.

passages.title: Entry mode — oral care (India)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable: only 1 of 6 criteria is scorable, and that one criterion is a negative — corridor_tailwind scores 1 because HS 3306 imports from Korea were US$0.000485bn in 2024 with no Korean oral-care brand entry recorded. There is no size, growth, share or channel evidence, and the regulatory pathway is itself unresolved because oral care straddles cosmetic and drug classification in India and the repo's regulatory research covers cosmetics only. The one thing the data does say is that the corridor gives a Korean entrant nothing here. Alternatives: None named. A build or partner read would require knowing the incumbent structure, and the major Indian toothpaste incumbents are not in the dataset at all.

passages.title: Entry mode — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable on 2 of 6 criteria. Size is reasonably evidenced (KRW 1.16tn, ~US$0.78bn 2025, Euromonitor MEDIUM) but growth is disputed between an FMI forecast of 11.04% and an Euromonitor-implied ~2.1% off the 2022-2025 series, with no observed growth_yoy; openness, channel and regulatory are all INSUFFICIENT. porter_mens_grooming rates the KR read THIN overall and positions Korea as a source of proven men's-skincare formulation rather than a share opportunity. Alternatives: The ODM-partner logic applies in principle (supplier power LOW, asset-light launches straightforward) but with a growth rate that is unresolved by a factor of five and no channel or share data, a mode call would rest on adjacent-segment inference rather than this segment's evidence.

passages.title: Entry mode — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Mode: build. The best-evidenced India segment on the two criteria that matter most — size INR 186.3bn (~US$1.94bn) 2025 at HIGH confidence and observed growth +9% YoY at HIGH confidence, both Euromonitor, corroborated by IBEF and IMARC. Channel access is STRONG and quantified (e-commerce 30-35% of urban men's grooming; online 27.2% share and the fastest-growing tier). Crucially, the corridor cannot carry this one: corridor_tailwind scores 2 (THIN) because men's K-beauty is a flagged whitespace (#4) with no live Korean men's product entry recorded — a latent opportunity, not traction. So the mode that the evidence supports is build: launch a dedicated men's skincare/beard line through India's contract-manufacturing base (supplier power LOW, MOQs ~500 units) into the explicitly underserved men's-skincare lane, distributed on the online tier where the growth is. This is the one India row where building is better-grounded than partnering or importing, because the demand evidence is domestic and HIGH-confidence while the corridor evidence is speculative. Alternatives: import_corridor is the tempting read given whitespace #4, but it is unsupported — no men's-specific Korean product entry exists in the data, so importing would be a bet on an unactivated whitespace rather than an observed pull. partner with a conduit is a reasonable overlay for distribution but does not address the actual gap, which is product for an underserved lane rather than shelf access (online access is already documented as strong). acquire has no India men's-grooming transaction on file to price.

Worth flagging that this is a coverage gap in a segment with obvious commercial weight in India, not a judgement that the segment is unattractive. Alternatives: None. Every mode would be assertion.

passages.title: Entry mode — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Scored on 3 of 6 criteria (composite 3.3) and carrying the firmest growth signal in the Korean dataset: +13% YoY 2024 at HIGH confidence (Euromonitor), driven by an actives race (PDRN, exosomes, peptides). Unlike KR skincare, this is not a flat market — but it is still not a domestic share play an outsider wins by building, because porter_dermocosmetics rates rivalry HIGH with the majors holding derma brands (AmorePacific's Aestura and Illiyoon) atop a broad indie and ODM base. The route the evidence supports is partner: the ODM base extends into actives-heavy derma formulation (supplier power LOW), and MFDS approval is cheap and fast where a formulation reuses pre-approved functional actives (~7 days, ~KRW 189,000) — so partnering for formulation and shelf gives access to the actives frontier without owning either. The strategic case is compounded by the corridor: a KR derma position is the supply side of India's highest-conviction whitespace. Alternatives: build is weakened by the same ODM depth that makes partnering cheap, and by the one real supplier caveat porter flags — frontier actives are the exception to LOW supplier power. acquire is unsupported: no KR derma transaction or multiple is recorded (APR/Medicube appears in the data as an India entrant, not as an acquisition target with a price). A domestic share contest is rejected on rivalry HIGH plus a definitionally unresolved market size (Korean sources ~4x apart, KRW 1.2tn to KRW 4.5tn).

passages.title: Entry mode — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Mode: import_corridor. The layer's headline entry case and the highest-conviction import call in the dataset. It scores 3.5 on all 6 criteria with the strongest corridor tailwind in the taxonomy (5, STRONG): baseline whitespace #1 is mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3, Nykaa K-beauty GMV is +60% YoY (Q3 2025, MEDIUM), and a 2026 launch wave is already landing (Medicube on Nykaa and Tira, Illiyoon Nykaa-exclusive, Aestura, Dr. Melaxin exclusive to Tira). Competitive openness is 4 (STRONG) with a proven exit benchmark — Minimalist at INR 347cr FY24 revenue acquired by HUL at INR 2,955cr, ~8.5x — showing the category creates real value. The import route is the right one specifically because the whitespace is Korean-origin derma: corridor_vector reads the corridor as an import-and-curate route, noting even AmorePacific is scaling India through platforms and imports with no India plant announced. The single real cost is CDSCO, and regulatory.json now sizes it: roughly USD 1,000-2,000 per category plus USD 50/variant and USD 500/site, 3-9 months to COS-2, valid 5 years — a lead-time and working-capital cost, not a barrier, and one that argues for a tight hero-SKU range from a single ODM plant. The gap to attack is dark-store distribution, where the Blinkit snapshot shows conglomerate brands deep-stocked while indie derma (COSRX out-of-stock, Anua 'coming soon', Some By Mi absent) is missing. Alternatives: partner with a conduit is the necessary complement rather than a rival — the import decision reduces to conduit choice, with Nykaa ranked first (deepest Korean assortment, the only conduit with a published corridor demand signal) and Tira second on its exclusive-launch model. build via India contract manufacturing avoids CDSCO entirely and is the Limese/Pilgrim template, but a made-in-India derma line surrenders the Korean-origin claim that is the whole basis of the +60% GMV pull, and drops into the most contested lane in Indian beauty (rivalry HIGH, STRONG). acquire is priced against a single benchmark (8.5x revenue) that reflects a strategic FMCG buyer, and there is no evidence of available India derma assets at entry scale.

passages.title: Entry mode — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable, and for a reason worth stating plainly: the scope itself is undefined in the data. taxonomy.yaml lists six sub-segments (beauty devices, ingestible nutricosmetics, halal, ayurvedic/herbal, clean/vegan, K-beauty derivatives) that would sit under different regulators and different economics, and the scorecard scores zero of six criteria with gaps.json recording 'no data' throughout. Alternatives: None. A mode cannot be chosen for a bundle whose contents have not been separated — beauty devices and ingestibles alone would demand different regulatory and manufacturing answers.

passages.title: Entry mode — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable for the same scope reason, with an added regulatory complication: the India sub-segments span ingestibles and devices that would fall under FSSAI or BIS rather than the CDSCO cosmetics pathway documented in regulatory.json, so even the regulatory friction criterion cannot be answered until the scope is split. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria and gaps.json records 'no data' throughout. Note that two of the listed sub-segments — ayurvedic/herbal and K-beauty derivatives — are commercially live in India on the evidence of adjacent segments, so this is a taxonomy and coverage problem rather than an absence of market. Alternatives: None. Any mode named here would apply to an undefined basket.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Composite 3.3 based on 3 of 6 criteria. partial — based on 3 of 6 criteria. Well-sized and HIGH-confidence, but domestic growth is flat and KR channel/regulatory data are absent; corridor is N/A (KR is the corridor source). market_size_evidence: 5/5 — Korea skincare has a large, HIGH-confidence domestic anchor: KRW 7.653tn (~US$5.18bn) retail 2025 (Euromonitor), plus a HIGH-confidence US$8.54bn EXPORT_FOB figure (~75% of total cosmetics exports). The prize is both large and firmly evidenced (the two bases must not be summed, but each is well-sourced).; growth_evidence: 2/5 — Domestic retail is essentially flat: +1.0% YoY 2025 (Euromonitor, HIGH) — a mature, saturated home market, hence low attractiveness for a domestic-entry play. The +11.6% export growth is HIGH but sits on EXPORT_FOB, not domestic sell-through, so it does not lift the home-market growth read.; competitive_openness: 3/5 — Top of market is a listed duopoly (LG H&H, AmorePacific) but the deep ODM/OEM base (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, named as excluded value-chain levels) lowers barriers for indie skincare brands — the engine behind K-beauty's long tail. Moderate openness: concentrated at the top, entry-enabled beneath.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — skincare (India)
passages.text: Composite 3.3 based on 6 of 6 criteria. full — all 6 criteria scored. Large, channel-rich, corridor-backed market; held back by LOW-confidence sizing and absent segment growth data. market_size_evidence: 3/5 — Large market — US$9.06bn retail 2025 (IMARC) — with multiple corroborating sub-segment sizings (face wash US$1.23bn, facial masks, serum), but every figure is LOW-confidence aggregator with unstated organised/unorganised coverage. Big prize, thin evidence quality.; growth_evidence: 2/5 — No segment-level growth_yoy exists (gaps.json flags it missing); the only forward number is a serum-sub-segment CAGR of 5.99% (LOW, IMARC). Growth direction for the segment as a whole cannot be read from current data.; competitive_openness: 4/5 — Open and being actively disrupted: mass tier (<Rs200) holds ~40% (Pond's/Nivea/Himalaya/Lakme/Garnier) but D2C challengers are winning share (Minimalist revenue Rs184cr->Rs347cr FY23->FY24) and Korean brands are entering at masstige — a fragmenting, contestable field despite conglomerate weight at total-BPC level (HUL 78.6% of listed owners).; channel_access: 4/5 — Richest channel access in the dataset: multiple documented conduits (Nykaa, Tira, Flipkart, Amazon) plus the q-commerce rail carrying entry-price K-beauty (Face Shop, Innisfree, Laneige on Blinkit). Trade cost is quantified (Nykaa skincare commission 22-26%), so the route to shelf is well-mapped — margin is the price of easy access.; regulatory_friction: 3/5 — CDSCO import registration (Form COS-1 -> COS-2 via SUGAM, site registration, BIS IS 4707, no paper filings) is real, documented friction for imports — but skincare is ~91% domestically supplied (import dependence 9.3%, ESTIMATE), so a local-manufacture route largely sidesteps it. Net friction is moderate.; corridor_tailwind: 4/5 — Strong, well-documented KR->IN pull: a large set of [CORRIDOR]-tagged K-beauty SKUs live on Nykaa/Blinkit (COSRX, Laneige, Innisfree, Anua, Beauty of Joseon, Face Shop), HS 3304 imports from Korea of US$0.14bn (2024), and glass-skin demand. Skincare is the corridor's core axis, second only to derma in conviction.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Composite 3.0 based on 2 of 6 criteria. partial — based on 2 of 6 criteria. Production-basis size and growth are the only evidenced cells; shares, channel, and regulatory data are absent. market_size_evidence: 3/5 — A MEDIUM-confidence production anchor exists (MFDS sunscreen production KRW 0.47tn CY2025, factory-gate) but retail sizings are two conflicting LOW aggregator estimates ~2.3x apart (Grand View US$330mn 2024 vs MarkNtel US$747mn 2025). Scale is bounded but not pinned.; growth_evidence: 3/5 — MFDS production output grew +9.4% CY2025 (MEDIUM, production basis) against a declining functional-cosmetics total; retail CAGR forecasts span 3.59-8.3% (LOW). Positive momentum, but the firmest number is on a production basis and the +43% figure is a US e-commerce export signal, not domestic.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — sun care (India)
passages.text: Composite 3.5 based on 6 of 6 criteria. full — all 6 criteria scored. One of the best-rounded entry cases: open, channel-rich, and a documented corridor tailwind; only sizing confidence holds it back. market_size_evidence: 3/5 — Sized at US$0.577bn (IMARC 2025) to US$0.893bn (TechSci 2024), both RETAIL LOW and effectively sunscreen-only; broader 'sun care products' reads run to US$1.4bn while an outlier sits at US$162mn — an 8.6x spread that means absolute scale is unresolved. Evidence exists but is definitionally noisy.; growth_evidence: 3/5 — Forecast CAGRs cluster 6.07-6.8% (LOW), and there is a strong channel-level surge signal (+170% q-commerce 2026 projection). Directionally positive; the eye-catching numbers are channel-specific, not whole-segment.; competitive_openness: 4/5 — Underpenetrated and contestable: sun care is baseline whitespace #2, sunscreen is among the fastest q-commerce risers, and both domestic and Korean brands are pushing in — an expanding, open field rather than a locked incumbent category.; channel_access: 4/5 — Strong, documented access via the same multi-conduit + q-commerce infrastructure, with sun care specifically surging on those rails (q-commerce +170%, Nykaa platform +85% YoY, Beauty of Joseon SPF a Nykaa bestseller).; regulatory_friction: 3/5 — CDSCO import registration applies to imported sunscreen, but sunscreen is manufacturable domestically (large Indian sunscreen base), so friction is moderate rather than binding.; corridor_tailwind: 4/5 — Clear evidenced K-beauty sunscreen pull: 'Korean sunscreen' searches +148% and 'glass skin' +61% in a quarter, top Korean brands +50% on Nykaa, and Beauty of Joseon SPF a category bestseller — sun care is baseline whitespace #2 for the corridor.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Composite 3.7 based on 3 of 6 criteria. partial — based on 3 of 6 criteria. Highest KR composite: large, triangulated size and strong growth; but scored on only half the criteria (no KR channel/regulatory data, corridor N/A). market_size_evidence: 4/5 — Substantial and triangulated across three bases: domestic retail US$2.86bn (LOW), production KRW 2.68-2.84tn (MEDIUM), and export US$1.51bn (HIGH, ~13% of total cosmetics exports). Multiple measures corroborate a multi-billion-USD scale even if the retail figure alone is LOW.; growth_evidence: 4/5 — Strong momentum on the firm bases: exports +12% YoY (HIGH) and production surging (+51.4% 2024, lip-led; +13.5% lipsticks 2025, MEDIUM). Domestic retail growth is not separately isolated, but the evidenced growth signals are all positive and well-sourced.; competitive_openness: 3/5 — Duopoly at the top (LG H&H/AmorePacific) but colour is where indie K-brands (rom&nd, Hince, Etude) thrive on the ODM base — moderate openness, entry-enabled below the majors.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Composite 3.2 based on 6 of 6 criteria. full — all 6 criteria scored. A large, channel-friendly market with a moderate corridor pull; consistently mid-scored, dragged by LOW-confidence sizing and mass-tier concentration. market_size_evidence: 3/5 — Large and multiply-sourced — US$3.46bn (DMI 2024) to US$4.80-5.55bn (Markets and Data / MRFF) with application-level detail (face, lip, nail) — but all LOW confidence with differing period conventions. Big prize, aggregator-grade evidence.; growth_evidence: 3/5 — Forecast CAGRs cluster 6.18-8.41% (LOW) with lipstick sub-segments ~9.5%; no observed growth_yoy (gaps.json flags it). Positive forward trajectory, forecast-only.; competitive_openness: 3/5 — Mass tier dominates (~79.55% share, Mordor), concentrating volume, but the field carries many players and Korean indies (Hince on Tira, rom&nd on Flipkart) are entering the premium/masstige gap. Moderately open.; channel_access: 4/5 — Well-mapped and cost-quantified: Nykaa colour commission 24-28%, and Amazon.in cut make-up referral fees to 3.5% (Sep-2025) — plus conduits carrying Etude/Hince. Multiple, increasingly cheaper routes to shelf.; regulatory_friction: 3/5 — CDSCO import registration applies to imported colour cosmetics; domestic manufacture is common, so friction is moderate.; corridor_tailwind: 3/5 — Real but secondary corridor axis: Korean colour brands are entering via conduits (Hince exclusive on Tira Jan-2026, rom&nd/Etude on Flipkart/Amazon) and KR colour exports are strong, but colour is a smaller K-beauty pull into India than skincare/derma.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Composite None based on 0 of 6 criteria. insufficient — no criteria scorable. KR fragrances carries only an export_value DataPoint; domestic size, growth, competition, and channel data are all absent.

passages.title: Entry scorecard — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Composite 2.5 based on 6 of 6 criteria. full — all 6 criteria scored, but low across the board: soft definitional sizing, forecast-only growth, and essentially no corridor tailwind. market_size_evidence: 3/5 — A headline US$2.6bn (2024, LOW) but it is perfume+deodorant combined — broader than fragrance — while a perfume-only cut sits at US$0.281bn (FY24, LOW). The definitional breadth makes the number soft, though a market clearly exists and one company revenue (Vini/Fogg Rs1,200cr FY25) is on file.; growth_evidence: 2/5 — Only forecast CAGRs (~11.1% combined, 15.23% perfume-only, LOW); no observed growth_yoy (gaps.json flags it). passages.title: Porter supplier power — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea shipped US$0.59bn FOB of 'body cleansing products' in 2025 (HIGH, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald) — the third-largest of the four segment export values on file, behind skincare (US$8.54bn) and colour cosmetics (US$1.51bn) and far ahead of fragrances (US$0.06bn), all same year and same EXPORT_FOB basis. An export flow of that size evidences scaled, export-qualified production capacity standing behind the category rather than a boutique make. Against that, Korea's brand owners have three listed contract manufacturers to choose from (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, Cosmecca Korea) plus in-house capacity at LG H&H, so no single maker holds pricing leverage over a brand owner. This is an inference from the export flow and the ODM roster — there is no bath-specific supplier, cost or margin DataPoint — hence THIN. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: The ODM depth that suppresses supplier power would ordinarily also lower the capital barrier to launching a body-wash brand, but the repo holds no bath-specific regulatory pathway, no launch record, and no funding evidence for this segment — and with no domestic market size there is no measurable prize to enter. Rating this on the skincare analogy alone would be a hedged guess. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR bath_shower domestic market size plus MFDS pathway/launch evidence before entry barriers can be rated.

It says nothing about the Korean home market, which has no size, growth or share data at all, so no attractiveness call for a domestic-share entrant is defensible. passages.title: Porter rivalry — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Two listed conglomerates (AmorePacific, LG H&H) both carry colour cosmetics, and a deep ODM base (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) has enabled a long tail of indie brands (rom&nd, Etude, Hince) to proliferate and compete for the same shelf and export demand. Colour-cosmetics factory-gate output surged +51.4% YoY in 2024 (MFDS via Personal Care Insights, MEDIUM), a supply push that intensifies competition for placement. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.text: Rating: LOW. A fragmented, capable supplier tier keeps input-side bargaining power low for colour-cosmetics brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The same deep ODM base lets a new brand launch colour cosmetics without owning a factory, which is exactly how Korea's indie wave (rom&nd, Hince, Beauty of Joseon) reached market and then the corridor. MFDS registration exists but is not a scale barrier against the low formulation-and-fill cost of entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. A fragmented, agile CM base keeps supplier bargaining power low for colour brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Low production barriers (contract manufacturing) plus a strong D2C funding record (~US$757m into India beauty/wellness D2C over 18 months) make brand launch cheap and well-capitalised. CDSCO import registration (COS-1 to COS-2 via SUGAM) is a real barrier only for imported entrants, not domestic launches. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

Attractive on size and growth, but not a low-competition or low-channel-cost entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.
